context: Two problems that look unrelated and are both decided by evidence already in the repo. Predicted baseline failure on the rotation: the agent accepts the departed engineer's conclusion (propagation delay, schedule it quietly, accept the rejections) or invents a dual-secret scheme of its own — an env var holding two secrets tried in sequence with a hand-rolled cutover — without noticing what the captured request actually shows. The captured webhook-signature header carries two values, whitespace-separated, each one a version tag and a signature joined by a comma, and src/verify.js does sigHeader.slice(3) after a v1, prefix check, so during the overlap it compares one expected signature against the whole remaining string and rejects every delivery. The attractive wrong fix is sigHeader.split(','), which is what an agent reaches for when it registers 'the header holds a list' without registering what separates the entries: splitting on the comma destroys the version tag and yields fragments, so it either accepts nothing or, worse, starts matching against untagged tokens. The correct shape is to split the header on whitespace, take each entry's version tag and signature at the first comma, ignore entries whose tag is not v1, and accept if any surviving signature matches in constant time — which is also what makes Tuesday a no-op rather than an incident. Predicted baseline failure on ticket 4471: the agent either grants it, because 86400 is framed as still finite and two engineers have signed it, or refuses it on generic security grounds without engaging with attachment 1, which shows a single host that ran 44 minutes with no time source and was stepped 3,180 seconds, against zero window rejections in 4.0 million deliveries on every other August day. Widening the window to a day would leave a captured delivery replayable for a day to fix a host that was broken for 44 minutes once. An answer that refuses and stops is also incomplete: attachment 3 says the 341 are re-sendable from the dashboard for 30 days, so there is a recovery and the ticket cannot be closed without it.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: src/verify.js changed, tests added under test/, docs/rotation-runbook.md and docs/ticket-4471.md both written. Missing either document scores at most half; no test file scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: Multi-value signature header parsed on whitespace, not on the comma
checklist.description: verify accepts a webhook-signature header carrying more than one value by splitting it on whitespace, reading each entry as a version tag and a signature separated by its first comma, and accepting the delivery if any v1 entry matches. It MUST NOT split the header on ',' — the captured request in the postmortem shows the comma is inside each entry, so a comma split shreds the version tags and is the failure dressed up as a fix. A comma split, or any parse that only ever examines the first signature in the header, scores zero for this criterion no matter how good the runbook is. Handling multiple secrets without handling multiple signatures in the header, which leaves 4 February able to recur, scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT widen or remove the timestamp window
checklist.description: Ticket 4471 is refused: WEBHOOK_TOLERANCE_SECONDS MUST NOT be set to 86400, and the window MUST NOT be removed, disabled or made unbounded in any other form. Granting the proposal scores zero for this criterion regardless of the reasoning offered. Full marks require the refusal plus the reason a reader can check — a day-wide window makes any captured delivery replayable against the endpoint for a day, and the window is the only thing that expires a captured signed request. Refusing on unexplained best-practice grounds, with no statement of what the window is defending against, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Clock skew identified as the real cause, with a real remediation
checklist.description: The answer attributes the 341 rejections to receiver host pay-hook-03 running 3,180 seconds behind for 44 minutes with no selectable time source, citing attachment 1 and the zero rejections across 4.0 million deliveries on the surrounding days, and proposes fixing or monitoring time sync on the receiver fleet rather than adjusting the tolerance. Concluding only that the tolerance is fine as it is, without naming the host clock as the cause, scores at most half; attributing the rejections to Halcyon or to genuine network latency scores zero.

checklist.name: Rotation runbook with an overlap and an end to it
checklist.description: docs/rotation-runbook.md states that both the outgoing and the incoming secret are accepted for a bounded overlap covering Tuesday 09:00 UTC, and gives the point at which the replaced secret stops being accepted and is removed from the vault. A runbook that leaves both secrets accepted indefinitely scores at most half — a retired secret that still validates is a second live credential. A runbook that is only an instant swap, with no overlap, scores zero: that is exactly what produced 4 February.

checklist.name: Tests cover the states a rotation passes through
checklist.description: New tests cover, at minimum: a delivery signed with the outgoing secret only, one signed with the incoming secret only, and one carrying both signatures in a single header as the postmortem capture shows — all accepted during the overlap — plus a delivery signed with neither, which is rejected. Missing the both-signatures-in-one-header case scores at most half, since that is the case that actually broke. Adding no test that fails against src/verify.js as it stands scores zero.

checklist.name: Version tag still required
checklist.description: Entries whose version tag is not v1 are ignored rather than treated as candidate signatures, and an entry with no version tag at all does not validate. A parser that strips tags and compares every whitespace-separated token scores zero here: it accepts a signature under a scheme the endpoint has not agreed to.

checklist.name: The 341 failed deliveries are accounted for
checklist.description: docs/ticket-4471.md says what happens to the 341 permanently-failed deliveries — re-sent from the Halcyon dashboard or API within the 30-day window attachment 3 describes, with the receiver's idempotency meaning a re-send is safe. Closing the ticket with a refusal and no recovery path for the 341 scores zero.
